claims.statement: 9% of orders allocated overnight to the east node have been held in 'allocated, awaiting pickup' for more than 90 minutes since 06:00; all other nodes are normal.
claims.corroboration: tier-1 verified monitor_alert from observability, single authoritative source sufficient for an observation of state.
claims.limitation: The alert measures state duration only; it explicitly cannot attribute a cause.

claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18, which makes multi-node orders reserve stock from the east node first, went live at 22:00 last night; change review passed and the regression suite was green.
claims.corroboration: tier-1 verified allocation_rule_record from the owning team (Inventory Control).
claims.limitation: Confirms the change occurred and passed review; does not by itself show the change is causing the stuck orders (temporal proximity is not causation).

claims.statement: Every currently-held order was routed to the east node and flagged by the overnight allocator as a split-reservation exception, with reports beginning around 06:00 and continuing.
claims.corroboration: m8_e10 is a single tier-2 non-authoritative source (customer_support), consistent with the tier-1 alert's east-node/06:00 pattern (m8_e02) and the timing of rule v18 (m8_e03), but not yet corroborated by an authoritative allocation-system record.
claims.limitation: Cannot yet be treated as root_cause: no discriminating evidence has isolated split-reservation exceptions from v18 as the mechanism versus carrier-side lag or dock capacity on the east node. Observability gap (m8_e09) means we also cannot rule out a carrier-confirmation mismatch. Support-report proxy counts do not establish customer impact.

next_action.rationale: C3's split-reservation-exception mechanism rests on a single non-authoritative support report. Auditing the allocation system's own exception records will confirm or deny whether the held east-node orders are in fact flagged as split-reservation exceptions by rule v18's logic, providing the discriminating, authoritative evidence needed to move toward (or away from) a root_cause claim of allocation_rule_defect, versus carrier_feed_lag or dock_capacity.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Authoritative confirmation of exception cause/rate tied to the held orders, distinguishing an allocation-rule defect from carrier- or dock-side explanations.
